CreateGameRequest.description:
Game creation payload (API-005).

``player_color`` and ``engine_level`` are the new-game choices for a
computer game; they are persisted on the row and drive whose turn is
enforced and how hard the engine searches. ``random`` resolves server-side to
a coin flip at the route before the row is written.
CreateGameRequest.title: CreateGameRequest

EmailRequest.description: An email address for a recovery request (verification resend / reset).
EmailRequest.title: EmailRequest

EngineMoveRequest.description:
Engine move payload (API-012).

Depth and time are no longer client-settable: the opponent's strength comes
from the game's difficulty (Phase 3), which the server maps to a bounded
search budget. The client only supplies the version it is playing against.
EngineMoveRequest.title: EngineMoveRequest

GameListResponse.description: A page of summaries plus the total, so the client can paginate.
GameListResponse.title: GameListResponse

GameResponse.description: A game with its move history (API-006/007).
GameResponse.title: GameResponse

GameSummaryResponse.description: A listable row from ``GET /games`` — no move payloads (API-006).
GameSummaryResponse.title: GameSummaryResponse

ReadinessResponse.description:
Readiness probe result (REL-007).

``engine`` reports the opponent backend (``builtin``/``local``/``up``/
``degraded``); it is informational and never makes the endpoint non-ready.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

RecoveryMessageResponse.description: Uniform, non-enumerating reply for a recovery request.
RecoveryMessageResponse.title: RecoveryMessageResponse

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Password-reset token plus the new password.
ResetPasswordRequest.title: ResetPasswordRequest

UserResponse.description: Public user representation (never includes password hash).
UserResponse.title: UserResponse

VerifyEmailRequest.description: Email-verification token submitted from the link.
VerifyEmailRequest.title: VerifyEmailRequest

post.description: Authenticate with email + password and start a session (SEC-004).
Revoke the current session; always clears cookies (SEC-005, idempotent).
Register a new account, start a session, and mail a verification link.
Send a password-reset link. The reply never reveals if the email exists.
Re-send a verification link. The reply is identical for any email.
Set a new password with a valid reset token and revoke all sessions.

Confirm an email address with a verification token (SEC-013).

The reply reflects token validity, not account existence, so it is safe to
distinguish success from an invalid/expired token.

get.description:
List the caller's games as a bounded page of summaries (API-006).

One aggregate query, no per-row move fetches: this replaces the N+1 that
used to call ``get_game`` for every row.

post.description:
Create a game in the starting position (API-005).

``random`` colour is resolved here so the persisted row records a concrete
side; a computer game where the player draws Black returns with the engine's
opening already played.

get.description: Fetch one game; 404 for unknown or foreign games (API-007).

post.description: Claim a draw when the position supports it (API-011).

Ask the configured engine to play one ply (API-012).

Strength is no longer client-controlled; the server maps the game's
difficulty to a bounded budget and falls back to the custom engine if the
primary backend is unavailable, so this never returns a silent 500.

get.description:
Download the game as PGN text (API-020).

Returns ``text/plain`` with an attachment disposition so browsers save it as
``game-<id>.pgn`` rather than rendering it.

schema.title: Response Health Api V1 Health Get

get.description: Report readiness: 200 when the database is reachable, else 503 (REL-007).
Aggregate wins/losses/draws by mode, from one query (API-021).
